question: Hawa Mahal is situated in which city?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Location and Design:** Hawa Mahal, also known as the "Palace of Winds," is located in Jaipur, the capital city of Rajasthan, India.

 
 
• It was designed in the form of the crown of Lord Krishna, with its unique five-story exterior resembling a honeycomb.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance: **Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, Hawa Mahal is an architectural marvel that is an integral part of Jaipur's history and royal heritage.
 
 
• It was constructed to enable ladies of the royal household to watch the life and processions of the city without being seen from the outside, given the strict "purdah" system followed at that time.
 
 
 
• **Architecture:** Hawa Mahal is a prime example of Rajput architecture and Indian artistry with its pink sandstone construction.
 
 
• The building does not have a foundation, and it is the tallest building in the world that does not have a solid base. It has over 950 windows, known as 'Jharokhas,' decorated with intricate latticework.
 
 
 
• **Ventilation: **The name "Hawa Mahal" translates to "Palace of Winds," which refers to the natural ventilation system in the building.
 
 
• The unique design of the windows allows cool air to circulate naturally through the building, making it an early example of sustainable architecture.
 
 
 
• **Tourism: **Today, Hawa Mahal is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Jaipur. Visitors can climb to the top floor for a panoramic view of the city, including the Jantar Mantar and the City Palace on one side and the Siredeori Bazaar on the other.
 
 
• It's a great place to learn about the culture and history of Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:** The Hawa Mahal is maintained by the Archaeological Department of the Government of Rajasthan.
 
 
• The monument is well-preserved, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the region, despite being over two centuries old.
